content:
raj: noticed a sudden customer spike of 503s across hosted-api at ~2024-08-03 17:02 UTC. multiple affected customers, p95 latency shot up. throwing to eng-sre/infra. logs show upstream inference worker died repeatedly.

elaine: oncall, looking. can you paste the runtime exit logs and the gateway traces?

raj: pasted snippet from router logs + worker stderr
```
2024-08-03T17:02:11Z worker-xy: pid=23456 exit_code=139 SIGSEGV
stack: libtorch::attention::dispatch +0x1a3
cuda assert: invalid device pointer
context: handling embed batch request customer=acme qps=350 batch_size=64 model=redwood-embed-2q
```
gateway:
```
2024-08-03T17:02:12Z gateway: upstream=10.4.5.62:8080 -> 503 (connection reset)
2024-08-03T17:02:12Z gateway: route=embed -> fallback to smaller-pool
```

simon: looks like GPU OOM or invalid pointer during prefetch/kvcache. any recent deploys? model swap? quantization change?

maria: CS reported customers saw streaming disconnects and retry storms. one customer had billing retries. open support ticket #4589.

raj: no prod deploys in last 30m. we did push a config tweak to prefetch concurrency yesterday that increased per-worker prefetch slots from 3 -> 6.

elaine: that change could amplify memory pressure during bursty embed loads. can you repro locally with a scaled embed stress test? steps?

raj: repro steps I ran in staging:
1) start 4 worker replicas with prefetch_slots=6
2) run embed-stress.py (320 qps, 64 batch-size, 4 concurrent clients)
3) after ~45s, worker shows cuda assert and exits

embed-stress snippet:
```
for i in range(8):
  client.embed(batch=64)
  sleep(0.2)
```

simon: ok will run that against a dev GPU pool. quick mitigation — roll back prefetch_slots to 3 on hosted pool and drain hot workers.

elaine: rolling back on hosted pool now. will also add an autoscaling cap to prevent >60% GPU mem saturation per worker.

deploy-bot: rollback deployment prefetch_slots -> 3 on pool hosted-embed-pool by elaine at 2024-08-03T17:09:04Z :white_check_mark:

maria: CS update queued: telling customers we saw an internal worker crash during embed bursts, mitigation in progress, ETA ~15m. customer billing team looped.

simon: dug into core dump: failure inside attention kernel when kv-prefetch memory map hits boundary. stack trace shows invalid pointer arithmetic when prefetch queue length >4. suspect race with kvcache resizing.

elaine: adding temporary rate limit on embed route to reduce concurrent prefetch windows until we patch the kernel. applying :no_entry_sign: 400 rps per-customer cap for embeds.

raj: confirmed gateway fallbacks removed once rollback completed. 503s dropped to normal baseline at 17:18.

maria: informing customer via ticket: "we identified upstream worker crashes during high embed concurrency caused by a prefetch concurrency regression; immediate rollback applied; mitigation: per-customer RPS cap and patch planned." :thumbsup:

simon: next steps
- reproduce reliably in CI with prefetch_slots=6
- write unit test for kvcache prefetch boundary
- produce hotfix for pointer arithmetic in attention kernel
- schedule canary deploy with extended memory telemetry

elaine: filing incident postmortem and action items. assigning owners: simon (bugfix), raj (ci repro), maria (customer comms). any other notes?

raj: add a retrospective note: consider safe defaults for prefetch/concurrency changes and a mandatory perf-cell signoff for memory-impacting flags.

infra-bot: incident ticket INC-2024-0823 created by elaine. severity=P2. sla impacted customers list attached.

maria: thanks team. will leave this thread open for follow-ups. :eyes:
